result.title: Termination Lag: Coding Agents Solve Early but Stop Late
result.summary: Coding agents can solve a task well before they stop working on it. We characterize \emph{termination lag}--the number of steps between an agent's first correct patch and the end of its run--across five models, two agent frameworks, and three SWE-bench datasets by recording and testing every distinct repository patch generated during execution. Our analysis reveals that 38--82% of successful runs achieve a correct solution on their initial source-code edit. However, agents continue to expend substantial effort after correct patches, with post-solution steps accounting for a median of 35--37% for Qwen3-Coder and 54--60% for Laguna-XS.2 in successful runs on SWE-bench Verified and Multilingual. Agents spend most of these additional steps verifying their work and exploring the repository. In a small fraction of cases (1--8%), this continued activity leads agents to undo their earlier correct patch, leaving the final solution incorrect.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在五个模型、两个 agent 框架和三个 SWE-bench 数据集上记录并测试执行中的每个仓库补丁，刻画「终止滞后」——首次出现正确补丁到运行结束之间的步数，发现大量成功运行在第一次代码编辑即已解决任务，却仍耗费大量步数做验证和仓库探索，少数情况下还会撤销此前的正确补丁。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作把「何时停止」与事后验证的成本显式量化，并提出「继续活动反而破坏已正确结果」的失败模式，可能为 VLM 推理中 STOP 的收益—成本核算与过度验证诊断提供问题表述，但需核查其纯代码任务设定能否迁移到多模态 latent 推理。
